summary.headline: 360 ONE WAM FY26 PAT rose 20.7% to Rs 1,225 crore, with ARR revenue at Rs 2,289 crore (up 34.5%) and total ARR AUM up 26% to Rs 3.12 lakh crore.
summary.overview: FY26 was the company's highest full-year PAT at Rs 1,225 crore, up 20.7%, and total revenue rose 18.6% to Rs 3,144 crore. ARR revenue reached 75% of revenue from operations, with organic ARR net flows up 36% to Rs 35,199 crore. Transaction and broking revenue rose 4.4% for the year but jumped 53.7% in Q4 to Rs 230 crore, helped by full-quarter consolidation of 360 ONE Capital (ex-B&K Securities). Management reset its transaction revenue run-rate guidance upward to Rs 170-180 crore per quarter, and guided to 15-25% profit growth on Wealth for the coming years.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 35,199 crore (Wealth Rs 25,900 crore; AM Rs 9,299 crore)

financial_highlights.change: up 34.5% YoY; 75% of revenue from operations

financial_highlights.metric: Transaction and broking revenue Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.change: Q3 was 49.5% on cost to total operating income basis

segments.name: Wealth (UHNI)
segments.commentary: UHNI cost-to-income stable at 44-45%; Wealth organic net flows Rs 25,900 crore in FY26. Management targets 12-15% of opening AUM as annual net flows and 15-25% Wealth profit growth.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.commentary: AM ARR AUM about Rs 95,000 crore; FY26 organic net flows Rs 9,299 crore. Q4 gross flows about Rs 5,200 crore, but net flows were about Rs 2,300-2,400 crore after about Rs 2,500-2,600 crore of maturities and distributions. Discretionary PMS flows have been soft.

segments.name: 360 ONE Capital (ex-B&K Securities)
segments.commentary: Full-quarter consolidation lifted Q4 TBR. B&K top line was about Rs 220-250 crore in the prior year, rising about 3-4% in the latest period, with PBT of about Rs 105-110 crore before acquisition costs. Investment banking build-out expected to contribute in 12-18 months.

segments.name: HNI reserve program
segments.commentary: About 60-65 RMs across 12 locations at closing, managing close to Rs 4,000 crore for 650-plus clients at about 90 bps yield. Management says revenue lags because the broker code change affects revenue only after 12 months.

segments.name: ET Money
segments.commentary: Undergoing strategic and business-model transformation; management expects breakeven in the near term without a specific timeline.

segments.name: Lending
segments.commentary: Largely Lombard / loan against shares, collateralised at 2x. Management reports no NPA and no loss since 2016; margin funding book under Rs 50-60 crore.

segments.name: Alternates carry
segments.commentary: Carryable AUM about Rs 30,000-35,000 crore; carry accrual 5-7 bps in a bad year and 12-15 bps in a good year. Modelling assumption of about 10 bps carry, so about 95-100 bps total Alternates yield.

guidance_outlook: Wealth: target net flows of 12-15% of opening AUM annually; AUM growth of 20-25%; RM count growth of 25-30% a year over the next 3-4 years; Wealth profit growth 15-25%. Management said it may add 25-35 RMs this year.
Cost-to-income: long-term target of 46-48% on the overall business ex-new businesses, and 45-47% over 2-3 years; UHNI/AM core stays at 44-45%.

Transaction and broking revenue: run-rate now seen at Rs 170-180 crore per quarter (earlier Rs 125-130 crore); aspiration north of Rs 200 crore. Management said the Rs 175-200 crore range is not cast in stone and later suggested Rs 160-180 crore.
Equity and equity-related income (ex-banking) expected to nearly double over 3-4 years; equity research revenue on Wealth side of Rs 85-90 crore a year could double or triple in 3-5 years.
Banking: 12 senior investment professionals to hire, about 4 in place; management expects to be more competitive over the next 3-4 months.
Tangible ROE expected to improve as Lending and Alternates capital turns into earnings.
Management expects 2-4% attrition a year and aims to double market share over 3-5 years.
capex_capacity: Senior relationship managers: about 180-190 currently; target 330-340 (team leaders from about 70-75 to 120-130; partners from 110-120 to about 240).
UHNI RM count about 63-64 at closing (about 35-40 on an average basis during FY26), with plans to go to 25-35 extra RMs in FY27.
Wealth market share estimated at 8-10%, with about 4,500 families above Rs 10 crore; target 8,000-10,000 families.
Alternates: 15-20 investment professionals per strategy; Lending with a dedicated team since 2016.
demand_pricing: Organic ARR net flows FY26 Rs 35,199 crore, of which Q4 net flows were about Rs 9,000-10,000 crore: advisory about Rs 4,500-5,000 crore, AM about Rs 2,000-2,500 crore, distribution and lending about Rs 2,000-2,500 crore.

Q4 AM gross flows about Rs 5,200 crore (FY26 about Rs 19,000 crore). Net flows reduced by a large credit fund maturity (Rs 1,500-1,700 crore), a real estate fund maturity (about Rs 850 crore) and a 2021-vintage PE fund distribution.

Discretionary PMS flows were softer than desired; the strategy is being pivoted and relaunched around early June 2026. Q4 DPMS retention was inflated by profit share on a small base. Negative distribution net flows of about Rs 212 crore were attributed mainly to corporate treasuries.
Management described 90% of cash segment share in broking, and over 500 mid- and small-cap companies under coverage.

Client base shift: family offices of about 400-500 clients (versus 40-50 five years ago); professionals now 15-20% of clients (from 5-10%); average ticket size rising due to a portfolio-based approach.

UBS collaboration: cross-referrals in NRI, resident and global mandates showing early traction. Regulatory approvals in GIFT City and on the UBS platform slowed progress; expected over the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 transaction revenue (UHNI TBR) so strong, and will the Rs 125-130 crore per quarter benchmark be revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TBR now looks closer to Rs 175-180 crore per quarter, helped by 360 ONE Capital and diversified asset-class mix (fixed income, REITs/InvITs, high-yield fixed income), and is more comfortable with Rs 170-180 crore than the earlier Rs 130-140 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 2 to 3 year yield (ex-carry) decline, and what is the carry model?
qa_highlights.answer: Yield ex-carry seen as broadly stable. Carry is accrued at about 10-14 bps a year on carryable AUM of about Rs 30,000-35,000 crore; modelling assumption is 10 bps carry, so about 95-100 bps Alternates yield.

qa_highlights.question: Is the guided 20-25% AUM growth and RM addition consistent with 15-25% profit growth, given cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost-to-income stays at 44-46% in the core UHNI and AM business, and operating leverage is high; it is willing to front-load RM hiring of 25-35 in FY27. Yield pressure and RM compensation are acknowledged but manageable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 1 April 2026 mutual fund yield cut hit B&K transaction revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is about 2-3% on a base of about Rs 200-225 crore a quarter, which is not material, and is offset by synergies.

qa_highlights.question: Industry consolidation, competition, and attrition in UHNI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes the industry needs 3-4 or more large players but remains fairly consolidated for the next 3-4 years. It expects 2-4% attrition a year and sees 12-15% flows as doable.

qa_highlights.question: Quality of new clients, carry exits, and gross flows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said family office clients are growing and portfolio-based onboarding raises ticket sizes. Sanjay Wadhwa gave AM gross flows of about Rs 5,200 crore in Q4 and Rs 19,000 crore in FY26. Management said the fund-level carry list would be compiled later in a data book.

risks_watch: Execution risk as headcount scales: management calls execution the biggest risk, with about 1,800 employees and plans to add 25-35 UHNI RMs in FY27 while senior RM count moves from about 180-190 toward 330-340.

RM war for talent and compensation: management says it will hire between the 90th and 110th compensation percentile, and says cost-to-income could drift up during hiring; FY26 cost-to-income was 49.9%.
Wealth flow delivery: the 12-15% of opening AUM net flow target is described as a tall order, and management flagged that it gets harder as size increases.
Discretionary PMS outflows and pricing: DPMS flows are soft, the strategy is being pivoted with relaunch around early June 2026, and Q4 DPMS retention was inflated by profit share on a small base.

Alternates and carry: AM Q4 net flows were hit by a credit fund maturity (Rs 1,500-1,700 crore), a real estate fund maturity (about Rs 850 crore) and a 2021-vintage PE distribution; carry accrual depends on hurdle performance and market variation.

B&K/360 ONE Capital: the MF yield cut from 1 April 2026 (about 2-3% impact on Rs 200-225 crore quarterly base), TBR sustainability, and banking hiring (12 professionals, about 4 in place) with IB contribution expected in 12-18 months.
UBS collaboration and GIFT City regulatory approvals slowed progress; management expects movement over the next quarter.
key_quotes: And honestly, I think it's fair to say that the size of the industry does require at least 3-4 potentially more larger players.
We're investing heavily into middle management leadership depth.
So, yields ex of carry, actually, I'm not too worried about.
That's really where it is. So honestly, I agree with you on all the three points.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the UHNI and AM core, with cost-to-income of 44-45% and yield described as broadly stable, but cautious on TBR (called not fully in control) and openly acknowledging softer discretionary PMS flows and slower UBS approvals. Management was evasive on some specifics, deferring the carry fund list to a later data book and giving only broad ranges for B&K figures and the TBR run-rate, which it later revised downward from 175-200 to 160-180 crore.

25-35 extra UHNI RMs planned in FY27

growth.why: Guided Wealth profit growth of 15-25% and AUM growth of 20-25% over 3-4 years, backed by a planned senior RM ramp (about 180-190 to 330-340) and 25-35 extra UHNI RMs in FY27, though no revenue growth figure was given and Q4 AM net flows were soft.
